info.title: PostGrip Agent API
info.description: Canonical HTTP contract consumed by the PostGrip Agent SDKs. Workflow replay, request signing, archive streaming, and WebSocket framing remain SDK runtime concerns.

get.description: Returns a fixed ok status without touching the store. It needs no credential at all, so an uptime monitor can call it. (`refreshAgentSession` is also public, but its body carries a refresh token.)
Reports readiness along with current task, workflow, schedule, and namespace counts. Unlike the liveness probe this route requires a credential.

get.summary: List namespaces visible to the caller
get.description: Scoped to the tenant the credential resolves to, and narrowed further to the agent's namespace allow-list when called with an agent session.

post.description: Any tenantId in the body is ignored and replaced with the tenant the credential resolves to.

get.description: Filters by namespace, queue, type, and state within the caller's tenant, then sorts and paginates. The answer is a bare array; to read the next page, send `offset` (or `page_token`, which is the same numeric offset) advanced by the number of tasks already read. `limit` has no maximum; without it every matching task is returned. An unknown `state` or `order_by` answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST with a message that names the parameter.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: One task state. Any other value answers 400.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: `created_at`, `-created_at`, `updated_at` or `-updated_at`; a leading `-` sorts newest first. Without it, tasks keep insertion order. Any other value answers 400.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: A numeric offset, used only when `offset` is absent.

200.description: Tasks, as a bare JSON array with no envelope and no next-page token.

400.description: An unknown `state` or `order_by`. The message names the parameter and the accepted values.

post.description: Returns 202 with the created task. Any tenantId in the body is replaced with the tenant the credential resolves to. A payload that carries a plaintext credential is refused with 400 PLAINTEXT_SECRET_REJECTED and nothing is stored. A shell.exec or container.exec task names its secrets in a top-level secret_env instead, mapping environment variables to secrets in the executing Agent's local store, and is leased only to Agents that advertise task_secret_env (see EnqueueTaskRequest.payload). A `workflow:` task whose payload sets a search attribute that starts with `postgrip.` is refused with 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming the attribute; that prefix is reserved for attributes PostGrip sets, such as `postgrip.scheduleId`. Any `type` is accepted: a custom type is leased only by a client that polls for it (see EnqueueTaskRequest.type).

get.summary: List recent events for multiple tasks

get.description: A task belonging to another tenant is reported as 404 rather than 403, so identifiers cannot be probed across tenant boundaries.
Returns one stable cursor page of the task's event history in order -- lease, start, heartbeat, stdout, stderr, and terminal events. Follow nextCursor until it is absent to consume the snapshot.

post.description: Returns 202. Any tenantId in the body is replaced with the tenant the credential resolves to. An `id` already used by a live (active or paused) schedule answers 409 CONFLICT `schedule already exists`. The `id` of a deleted schedule can be used again: the new schedule replaces the deleted one, and the runs the deleted schedule started keep its `schedule_id` in their history.

patch.description: Only the top-level fields present in the body are changed. `spec` and `action` each replace the stored object whole, so an object that omits a member whose stored value it would change answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST, names those members (for example `invalid schedule: spec omits timezone, jitter_seconds; ...`), and changes nothing. Send every member with the value to keep, and send a member explicitly, with an empty value or null, to clear it. Defaults count as kept: an omitted `timezone` that is stored as `UTC`, `missed_run_policy` stored as `catch_up`, action `namespace` equal to the schedule's and `queue` equal to `default`. The timing mode (`cron`, `interval_seconds` or `calendar`) is never listed: the one the new spec names replaces the stored one.

400.description: The body is invalid, a field breaks a schedule rule, or `spec` or `action` omits a member it would reset. The message names the rule or the members.

delete.description: Returns the deleted schedule with 200 rather than an empty 204; the record moves to the deleted state. A later createSchedule with the same `id` replaces the deleted record.

post.description: Stops the schedule firing without deleting it, and returns the updated schedule. The request's `reason` is accepted but not stored or audited.
The request's `reason` is accepted but not stored or audited.
Fires the schedule out of band from its spec. The next scheduled run is unaffected. The request's `reason` is accepted but not stored or audited.

post.summary: Backfill a schedule across a time range
post.description: Enqueues one task per scheduled instant between the requested start and end. A request enqueues at most 100 tasks: a range with more scheduled instants is truncated to its first 100 and still answers 202, so backfill a longer range in several requests.

get.description: Filters, sorts and paginates workflow executions within the caller's tenant; the answer is a bare array. Filter on a search attribute with `search.<name>=<value>`, or inside `query` as `search.<name>=<value>`. A run that a schedule emits carries the system search attribute `postgrip.scheduleId`, so `search.postgrip.scheduleId=<scheduleId>` lists that schedule's runs. Runs started any other way, and runs emitted before the attribute existed, do not carry it.

parameters.name: search.*
parameters.description: Search-attribute filter; replace * with the attribute name, for example `search.postgrip.scheduleId=<scheduleId>` for the runs a schedule emitted.

get.summary: Count workflow executions matching a filter
get.description: Applies the same filters as the list operation and returns only the count. Paging parameters are ignored.

parameters.name: search.*
parameters.description: Search-attribute filter; replace * with the attribute name, for example `search.postgrip.scheduleId=<scheduleId>` for the runs a schedule emitted.

get.description: Returns the latest run of the workflow.
Returns one stable cursor page for a single workflow run. Follow nextCursor until it is absent to consume the snapshot; a cursor remains bound to the original run if the workflow continues as new.

post.summary: Send a signal to a running workflow
post.description: Returns 202 with the appended history event. A signal also releases the workflow's blocked task, which is how a task that parked itself resumes. Signalling a workflow that is no longer running fails.

post.summary: Signal a workflow, starting it first if none is running
post.description: Starts a new execution of workflowType when no running one exists, then delivers the signal. A workflowId in the body takes precedence over the one in the path.

post.summary: Request cooperative cancellation of a workflow
post.description: Asks the workflow to stop at its next cancellation point. Use terminate for an execution that does not cooperate.
Stops the execution immediately, without giving workflow code a chance to clean up.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new agent session
post.description: The refresh token in the body is itself the credential, so this operation carries no bearer token. Rotation is single-use: presenting a token that has already been rotated revokes the whole token family.

get.summary: Long-poll for the next leased task or lifecycle directive
get.description: Blocks up to wait_seconds and returns 200 with an empty object -- not 204 -- when nothing is available. A queued lifecycle directive (upgrade, log level, attest) is returned in place of a task, and an agent that has been removed receives 410 carrying a shutdown directive.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Current agent runtime version used to enforce upgrade policy.

parameters.name: log_level
parameters.description: Current agent log level used to synchronize runtime configuration.

parameters.name: capabilities
parameters.description: Runtime and isolation capabilities advertised by the agent. The server accepts repeated or comma-separated values.

410.description: The agent has been removed. The body carries a shutdown directive and the agent should stop polling and exit.

post.description: Extends the lease and appends a heartbeat event. The task must currently be leased to the calling agent.

post.summary: Append an event to a leased task
post.description: Records one task event and returns 202. Agents send progress, milestone, stdout, and stderr; the TypeScript and Python workers additionally emit started, completed, and failed markers alongside the authoritative complete and fail calls, so a finished task can carry two completed events. Only the server writes leased. The kind is not validated -- an empty value defaults to progress. This does not extend the lease; send a heartbeat for that.
Terminal. Stores the result, releases the lease, and advances the owning workflow. Secret values drawn from the task's environment are masked out of the stored result.

post.summary: Park a leased task until its workflow is signalled
post.description: Non-terminal: the task moves to blocked and its lease is released, so it is not retried and no longer counts against the agent. A worker calls this whenever a workflow body suspends on a pending durable command -- an activity, a timer, a child workflow, or an awaited signal. The orchestrator re-queues the task for redelivery as soon as that dependency resolves: the activity completes, fails, or times out; the timer fires; the child workflow finishes; a signal or workflow update arrives; or the workflow is cancelled.
Terminal. Records the error, releases the lease, and drives the workflow's retry or failure handling. Error text is masked for secrets before it is stored.

get.description: Returns the tenant's live sandboxes. Deleted sandboxes are omitted here but remain fetchable by id.

post.description: Records the desired sandbox and returns 201. Provisioning is asynchronous, so the returned record is not yet running. Names must be unique per tenant among live sandboxes. The request answers 400 unless: `name` matches `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,62}$`; `architecture`, when set, is `amd64` or `arm64`; resource limits are non-negative, at most 4 CPUs and 4 GiB of memory, with disk between 64 MiB and 20 GiB; every port mapping has host and guest ports from 1 through 65535, protocol `tcp` (the default) or `udp`, and no host port repeats for a protocol; `backend` is not `firecracker` (no Agent can host it yet); `allowCidrs` is empty (CIDR allow-lists are not supported); `ports` are set only with `internetEgress` (without it the sandbox has no network); `internetEgress` is not combined with `denyHostAccess`; `workspaceId`, when set, names one of the tenant's workspaces; `expiresAt`, when set, is in the future and at most 24 hours ahead (it defaults to 24 hours).

delete.description: Sets desired state to deleted and returns 202 with the updated record. Teardown is asynchronous and completes when the assigned agent reports it.

post.description: Sets desired state to running and returns 202. The returned record still carries the previous observed state; a sandbox is ready only once observedState is running and observedGeneration has caught up with generation. Starting a `failed` sandbox raises its generation, so its Agent tries again (see Sandbox.observedState).
Sets desired state to stopped and returns 202. The assigned agent applies it asynchronously.

post.summary: Mint a single-use ticket for a sandbox stream
post.description: Creates a pending pty, exec, or port session and returns its ticket exactly once -- only a hash of it is stored. The ticket is short-lived and is redeemed against the connect operation. The sandbox must already be running. Port sessions require an advertised port-stream-capable agent and a TCP guest port that is already published by the sandbox. Pending and connected sessions are limited to 20 per tenant, 10 per agent, and 5 per sandbox; a limit breach returns 429.

get.description: Returns every workspace archive owned by the authenticated tenant, newest first.

post.description: The request body is a raw gzipped tar stream, not a multipart form. Repository and revision metadata travel in the X-PostGrip-Repository and X-PostGrip-Revision headers. Storage is content-addressed, so re-uploading identical bytes returns the existing record, with its first labels and its `expiresAt` renewed to 24 hours after this upload, rather than creating a new one. An expired workspace that no live sandbox uses is deleted (see SandboxWorkspace.expiresAt). A body that does not start a gzipped tar (an empty body, one without the gzip magic, or gzip whose first entry is not a tar header) answers 400 INVALID_REQUEST with `workspace archive must be a gzipped tar`, and nothing is stored. The Agent checks the remaining entries when it unpacks the workspace.

400.description: The body is not a gzipped tar.

delete.description: Deletes the tenant's workspace record and removes its archive once no tenant references the same content-addressed blob. A workspace still referenced by a live sandbox returns 409.

get.summary: Attach to an interactive session over WebSocket
get.description: Upgrades to the one-shot WebSocket stream authorized by the ticket. For pty and exec sessions, binary messages carry raw stdin/stdout bytes and stdout/stderr are interleaved. postgrip.sandbox.terminal.v1 reserves client-to-agent text frames for strict resize JSON of the form {"type":"resize","rows":24,"columns":80}; postgrip.sandbox.terminal.v2 applies strict JSON control framing in both directions and additionally permits agent-to-client notice messages of the form {"type":"notice","code":"session_ready","message":"Sandbox stream is ready"}. Rows and columns must be integers from 1 through 65535. A zero-length client binary message signals terminal stdin EOF without closing output. Without a negotiated terminal protocol, text messages remain legacy raw stdin. Exec exit codes, and only exec exit codes, use WebSocket close status 4000 plus the process code. For port sessions, postgrip.sandbox.port.v1 carries raw TCP bytes in binary messages; text messages are invalid, and terminal controls and terminal close-code semantics do not apply. Ping/Pong liveness is enforced independently on every proxy hop, and any failed hop terminates both relay peers. Refusals before the upgrade use the JSON error body: a missing, wrong, expired or already used ticket answers 404 NOT_FOUND with `session ticket is invalid, expired or already used`; a cross-origin browser request answers 403 FORBIDDEN; and a session whose client peer is already connected answers 409 CONFLICT.

postgripToken.description: Tenant-scoped PostGrip management token carrying concrete Agent, Worker, and Service grants. A pgt_ token that is unknown, revoked or expired answers 401 INVALID_TOKEN on every route, including routes that also accept an agent session. A valid token without the route's scope answers 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, with the scope in details.requiredScopes (an array) and, when the route needs a single scope, details.requiredScope (a string).

agentSession.description: Delegated short-lived agent session. Signed operations also carry the PostGrip Ed25519 request-signing headers. On a route that accepts both credentials, a bearer token without the pgt_ prefix is authenticated as an agent session, and a failing one answers 401 AGENT_UNAUTHORIZED.

AgentIdQuery.name: agent_id
AgentIdQuery.description: Compatibility identifier; authenticated requests derive the agent from the session token.

HistoryCursor.name: cursor
HistoryCursor.description: Opaque cursor returned as nextCursor by the preceding page.

HistoryPageLimit.name: limit
HistoryPageLimit.description: Maximum number of events in one response page. The server may return fewer items to honor its serialized response-size bound.

SandboxBackend.description: `firecracker` is reserved: create refuses it with 400, because no Agent can host it yet (none advertises it, so `auto` never resolves to it).

type.description: The task type. The built-in types are `noop`, `shell.exec`, `container.exec` and `workflow.runtime`, which PostGrip Agents run, and the `workflow:`, `activity:`, `query:` and `update:` prefixes the SDK workflow runtimes use. Any other value is accepted as a custom type: a client that polls with that type in `task_types` (see pollAgentTask) leases it, and PostGrip Agents never do. A task whose type nothing polls for stays `queued`; task cancellation, once available, will remove such a task.

payload.description: Task-type payload. The control plane stores payloads, so never put a credential in one: a payload with a credential-shaped key at any depth, URL userinfo in a key or value other than a bare account on an ssh or git URL, or a value that cannot be fully inspected is refused with 400 PLAINTEXT_SECRET_REJECTED. The one exception is the top-level secret_env object of a shell.exec or container.exec payload: its keys are environment variable names, which may be credential-shaped (PGPASSWORD), and every value must be the name of a secret in the executing Agent's local store (/run/secrets). The Agent resolves the values when the task runs, so only names are stored. A task with a non-empty secret_env is leased only to an Agent that advertises the task_secret_env capability, and one whose secret_env is not an object is leased to none.

type.description: The task type, as sent to enqueueTask (see EnqueueTaskRequest.type).

exit_code.description: The process's exit code. Omitted when the process exited 0, and when the task ran no process (a noop or workflow task, or a command that never started): read a missing value as 0, and the task's `state` and `error` for whether a process ran and why it failed.

searchAttributes.description: Copied to every run the schedule emits, and PostGrip adds `postgrip.scheduleId` with the schedule's id so the runs can be listed with `search.postgrip.scheduleId`. Names that start with `postgrip.` are reserved for attributes PostGrip sets; a request that sets one is refused with 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming the attribute.

search_attributes.description: The search attributes the run started with. Names that start with `postgrip.` are reserved for attributes PostGrip sets: a run a schedule emitted carries `postgrip.scheduleId` with that schedule's id. A caller cannot set a `postgrip.` attribute.

searchAttributes.description: Search attributes of the run this request starts. Names that start with `postgrip.` are reserved for attributes PostGrip sets; a request that sets one is refused with 400 INVALID_REQUEST naming the attribute.

internetEgress.description: Give the sandbox a network with internet access. Port mappings need it.

allowCidrs.description: Not supported yet: any non-empty value answers 400.

denyHostAccess.description: Not supported with `internetEgress`. Without it the sandbox has no network, so the host is unreachable anyway.

ports.description: Host-to-guest port mappings, published on the Agent's loopback. They need `internetEgress`.

SandboxNetworkPolicyInput.description: The network policy on create. Every member is optional: the booleans default to false, which gives the sandbox no network.

observedState.description: The state the sandbox's Agent last reported. `failed` means the Agent's last attempt to reach `desiredState` failed, and `failureCode` and `failureMessage` say why. The Agent tries a failed sandbox again with exponential backoff, about 30 seconds and then 1, 2 and 4 minutes after each failure, at most 5 attempts at the same `generation`. After the fifth, `failureMessage` ends with `(failed 5 times; not retried until the sandbox is started, stopped or deleted again)` and `failed` stays. Starting, stopping or deleting the sandbox raises `generation`, which gives it 5 new attempts; a restart of the Agent also starts the count again. When the request itself causes the failure, for example an image that cannot be pulled or a setup command that fails, delete the sandbox and create a corrected one.

credentialRefs.description: Not supported yet: any non-empty value answers 400.

port.description: Guest-side TCP port for kind=port; it must match a published sandbox network-policy mapping.

terminalProtocols.description: Terminal WebSocket subprotocols supported by the target agent and relay, in preference order. Present only for pty and exec sessions. Omitted by legacy orchestrators; clients must then connect without a subprotocol and keep the session's initial dimensions.

byteStreamProtocols.description: Raw byte-stream WebSocket subprotocols supported by this relay, in preference order. Present only for port sessions and never interpreted as terminal framing.

expiresAt.description: When the workspace expires: 24 hours after its last upload. Uploading the same bytes again returns the same workspace and moves `expiresAt` to 24 hours after that upload; it never moves it earlier. Within about a minute after `expiresAt`, PostGrip deletes the workspace and its archive, as `deleteWorkspace` does, unless a sandbox without a `deletedAt` uses it; such a workspace is kept while that sandbox exists and deleted at the next pass after the sandbox's `deletedAt`. A re-upload that arrives before the deletion keeps the workspace.
